introduction_markdown:
Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board, General Certificate of Education Examination, ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2019. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2, subject code 0575. Time allowed: two and a half hours.

Answer ALL QUESTIONS IN SECTION A and ANY TWO QUESTIONS FROM EITHER SECTION B or SECTION C. In Sections B and C, ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three.

Section A: Pure Mathematics (compulsory to all candidates, answer all questions). Section B: Mechanics (answer any two questions; if this section is chosen, then Section C may not be chosen). Section C: Statistics and Probability (if this section is chosen, then Section B may not be chosen; answer any two questions).

All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take $g$ as $10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the double-angle formulae $\cos2A=1-2\sin^2A$ and $\sin2A=2\sin A\cos A$.

$$
\frac{1-\cos2A}{\sin2A}=\frac{1-(1-2\sin^2A)}{2\sin A\cos A}=\frac{2\sin^2A}{2\sin A\cos A}=\frac{\sin A}{\cos A}=\tan A
$$

as required. $\blacksquare$

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) The function $g(x)=\cos2x-\sin x$, $0\le x\le\pi$.

(a) Copy and complete the table. *[2 marks]*

| $x$ | $0$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ | $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ | $\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ | $\pi$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $g(x)$ | $1$ |  |  | $-2$ |  |  | $1$ |

Taking $2$ cm to represent $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ radian units on the $x$-axis and $4$ cm to represent $1$ unit on the $y$-axis,

(b) Draw the graph of $y=g(x)$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Scales:** $x$-axis: $2$ cm per $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, so $x=0,\dfrac{\pi}{6},\dots,\pi$ are at $0,2,4,6,8,10,12$ cm. $y$-axis: $4$ cm per unit, so $y$ runs from $-2$ (at $-8$ cm) to $1$ (at $4$ cm).

**Points to plot** (distance in cm from the origin):

| $x$ | $0$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ | $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ | $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ | $\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ | $\pi$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $x$ (cm) | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ | $12$ |
| $g(x)$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-1.37$ | $-2$ | $-1.37$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| $y$ (cm) | $4$ | $0$ | $-5.5$ | $-8$ | $-5.5$ | $0$ | $4$ |

Join the points with a smooth curve. The curve starts at $(0,1)$, crosses the $x$-axis at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, falls to its lowest point $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2},-2\right)$, then rises symmetrically about the line $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, crossing the $x$-axis at $x=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$ and ending at $(\pi,1)$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
From your graph,

(c) Find the minimum value of $g(x)$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The lowest point of the curve is at $x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, where $g=-2$.

Check by algebra: $g(x)=1-2\sin^2x-\sin x$. With $s=\sin x\in[0,1]$, $g=1-s-2s^2$, which decreases as $s$ increases, so the minimum is at $s=1$ ($x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$): $1-1-2=-2$.

**The minimum value of $g(x)$ is $-2$.**
